page.layout: One page of text in one column, with the running head "AVGVSTINVS" and the page number "Cap.88." at the top. Verse quoted in italics in the middle of the text. Catchword at the lower right and signature at the lower left. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: itémque ab alio Pelagio, qui Tarentus dictus eft, noftro huic æqualis, fed orthodoxus. Illo vero feculo cœperat iam Britania in Gallia vocari ea Galliæ poftrema plaga, in quam Britâni (qui nunc Angli dicuntur) ex Albione infula,& è patriis fedibus partim à Maximo tyranno traducti fuerant, vt Martinus Polonus in fuo Chronico tradit, vt eorum imperium propagaretur: partim à Scotis populis, & Anglis (qui funt Saxonici populi) rege Vertunegaro duce, vt ait Pomponius Lætus, pulfi fuerant, quod fub Valentiniano fecundo accidit, ante hanc hærefin enatam. Nec mirum eft tam peftilentem errorem ab homine Britone excogitari fparfíque potuiffe. Illo enim feculo, vt docet Aufonius lepidiffimo epigrammate, mixti Gallis, profugi Britones ifti non nifi mali habebantur. Aufonij vero epigramma fic habet,

l.i: Siluius hic bonus eft: Quis Siluius iste Britannus? Aut Brito hic non eft Siluius, aut malus eft.

main_text.l: Quum autem egreffus Roma, peregrè ageret in Syria, Nouatianorum & Meletianorum, id eft, Operiftarum[?], qui plurimi in illis regionibus erant, veneno femel haufto, longius progreffus eft Pelagius, & operum merita, liberúmque hominis arbitrium Dei gratiæ repugnans, aperte induxit. Ex Nouatianorum enim fontibus ortum effe hûc errorem non dubito, potiùs quàm ex Manichæorum deliriis, quanquam Augustinus libro 4. ad Bonifacium, magnam effe Manichæorum & Pelagianorum in dogmatibus plerifque confenfionem docet. Habitus autem Pelagius pro fui feculi ratione non indoctus, &c

page.notes: The word "Operiftarum" in the Syria passage is uncertain; the reading "Operistarum" is my best guess and is marked [?]. The signature at the lower left is partly obscured, so "C" is doubtful. The catchword "libro" is clear. The page number "Cap.88." is printed at the head and is treated as the page number. Long s and the ct ligature in "dictus" were normalised as described in the rules, with "s" written as "s". The line "Nec mirum" continues the paragraph that began on the previous page. The Latin "libro 4." is kept as printed.
